edge.title: Radial brake: halve outward radial update, then pin post-step norm
edge.summary: Adds a radial brake to every hidden matrix on top of #20. After muon_update, the update u is split into a radial part (its projection onto the weight W) and a tangential part; if the step −lr·u would move W outward (⟨u, W⟩ < 0) the radial part is multiplied by 0.5 (inward motion untouched), and only then is the 0.3825 u/w floor applied. After the step, W is rescaled to ‖W‖ − lr·⟨u, W⟩/‖W‖, so the norm changes only by the first-order (braked) radial term and the second-order growth from the tangential step is removed. The run is shortened to 3020 steps (PowerCool endpoint still 3105) and claimed at 2990.

changes.label: Outward radial component × 0.5
changes.detail: scale_radial_update: coeff = ⟨u, W⟩/‖W‖²; radial = coeff·W is scaled by RADIAL_OUTWARD_SCALE = 0.5 if coeff < 0, else RADIAL_INWARD_SCALE = 1.0; applied before the u/w floor.

changes.label: Post-step radius pin
changes.detail: target_radius_after_update computes ‖W‖ − lr·⟨u, W⟩/‖W‖ from the floored update; after p.add_, rescale_to_radius multiplies W to exactly that norm, removing tangential norm drift.

changes.label: train_steps 3040 → 3020, claim 2990
changes.detail: FINAL_TRAIN_STEPS = 3020 with unchanged PowerCool constants and endpoint 3105; claimed at the 2990 checkpoint (Muon LR ≈2.6% of peak).

changes.label: Logging and validation grid
changes.detail: LOG_DIR = 'logs', UTC timestamp print, new intuition string, radial config prints, extra_val_steps {2990, 2995, 2999, 3000, 3010, 3020}.

mechanisms.name: Radial brake + radius pin
mechanisms.explain: The update u is decomposed into its component along the weight W (coeff = ⟨u, W⟩/‖W‖²) and the tangential remainder. Because the step is W ← W − lr·u, coeff < 0 means the weight would grow, and in that case the radial component is halved (RADIAL_OUTWARD_SCALE = 0.5) before the u/w floor; inward components are untouched. After the step, W is rescaled to ‖W‖ − lr·⟨u, W⟩/‖W‖ (the first-order radius change), removing the √(‖W‖² + lr²‖u_t‖²) norm creep caused by finite tangential steps, which the u/w-floor regime (no weight decay) would otherwise accumulate.

caveats: The README describes the damping as a post-step norm rescale; in code the outward radial part is halved on the update before the u/w floor, and the post-step rescale only pins the norm to the first-order prediction. When the u/w floor binds it rescales the whole braked update back up, so the brake then shifts step size from radial to tangential rather than shrinking the step. All #20 caveats carry over (attn.proj trust gate dormant, Schatten-4 norms, effective wd 0).
